First, regarding the use of the character designs at issue: after their creation, the Shanghai Animation Film Studio used them in the films at issue and subsequent films, published and distributed related audio-visual products, and also licensed others to use the character images at issue on bank cards. Meanwhile, before the public release of the films at issue, Qu Jianfang used the works at issue to publish comic strips and character illustrations in periodicals, and subsequently continued to submit the works at issue for external publication in public publications, used or authorized others to use the Effendi and other character images to produce animated films, and licensed the use of Effendi and other character images on product packaging, advertising, mobile animation projects, and other media. Second, regarding the parties' control over and assertion of rights in the character designs at issue: Qu Jianfang obtained the copyright registration certificate for the "Effendi" artistic work in 1996. Both the Shanghai Animation Film Studio and Qu Jianfang have asserted their rights by filing lawsuits against unauthorized use of the character images at issue by others, and have been recognized by relevant courts as the right holders of the character images at issue. There was a media report on a lawsuit heard by the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, where Qu Jianfang sued others for infringing his copyright by unauthorized use of the Effendi image. Prior to this lawsuit, the Shanghai Animation Film Studio and Qu Jianfang had never asserted rights against each other regarding the character images at issue. In particular, after jointly undergoing the trial of Case No. (2008) Pu Min San (Zhi) Chu Zi No. 449 of the Pudong New Area People's Court of Shanghai and after the Shanghai Animation Film Studio learned that Qu Jianfang had registered the copyright in the "Effendi" artistic work, it still did not assert rights against Qu Jianfang. Third, regarding the fame and connotative value of the character design works at issue: initially, they directly benefited from the Shanghai Animation Film Studio's investment in the films at issue and subsequent films, and their dissemination through audio-visual products and other forms. The awards won by the films at issue further enhanced the fame and value of the character designs at issue. Meanwhile, Qu Jianfang's continuous use of the works at issue in various ways not only enriched the connotation of the works at issue, but the awards won by the films he produced or authorized others to produce using the Effendi and other character design works at issue also contributed to enhancing the fame and value of the character designs at issue. Based on the above facts, during the period of over thirty years from the completion of the creation of the character design works at issue to the filing of this lawsuit by the Shanghai Animation Film Studio, the coexistence of the Shanghai Animation Film Studio and Qu Jianfang each using the works at issue was an objective fact. The Shanghai Animation Film Studio, knowing the above facts, never expressed objection nor proactively initiated relief procedures to assert rights against Qu Jianfang. This state of affairs was sufficient to lead Qu Jianfang to believe that he could exercise and control relevant rights as the copyright owner of the works at issue. Moreover, as mentioned above, Qu Jianfang's continuous control and use of the works at issue also contributed to the fame and connotative value of the works at issue. Therefore, under such circumstances, attributing the copyright property rights in the works at issue solely to one party would clearly lead to an imbalance of rights and violate the principle of fairness. The court of first instance, based on the parties' exercise of copyright in the works at issue and considering factors such as fairness and good faith, confirmed that the copyright property rights in the artistic works of the character designs at issue are jointly owned by the Shanghai Animation Film Studio and Qu Jianfang. This determination is not improper, and the court affirms it.

3. In light of the analysis and determination of the second issue above, the copyright property rights in the character designs at issue are jointly owned by the Appellant Shanghai Animation Film Studio and the Appellant Qu Jianfang. The Appellee Electronic Publishing House published the book at issue under the authorization of Qu Jianfang. Therefore, the reasons for the Shanghai Animation Film Studio's claim requiring Qu Jianfang and the Electronic Publishing House to bear tort liability cannot be established.

In summary, the grounds of appeal of both the Appellant Shanghai Animation Film Studio and the Appellant Qu Jianfang, that the copyright in the character designs at issue should belong solely to each of them, cannot be established. The trial procedure of the court of first instance was lawful, the facts were clearly found, the law was correctly applied, and the adjudication result was not improper. However, the court of first instance made an error in determining the acceptance fee for the counterclaim, which the court hereby corrects. Accordingly, pursuant to the provisions of Article 170, paragraph 1, subparagraph (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the court rendered a judgment on November 30, 2015:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
